insight: Cold drinks, ice, buttermilk, and dairy-based beverages often see increased local demand during the summer months.
Umbrellas, raincoats, hot beverages, and packaged snacks can see a local demand bump during the monsoon season.
Warm clothing accessories, hot snacks, and dry-fruit or ghee-based products may see increased demand in winter.
Sweets, dry fruits, ghee, and gifting-sized packaged goods typically see a local sales rise during festival weeks.
Festival season often brings a short-term rise in new clothing and alteration orders in the weeks before the festival.
Cash flow among farming households in Punjab can improve shortly after the wheat/paddy harvest and mandi sales, which may lift local retail demand.
Punjab has a strong dairy consumption base; bundling milk with related staples (tea, sugar, ghee) can support basket size.
Foot-traffic-dependent businesses often benefit from tracking local weekly market days, festivals, and school/college schedules that change footfall.
Local events, weddings, and school/college reopening dates can create short predictable demand spikes worth preparing stock for in advance.
